title: The Help: the Ref button paragraph into sub-bullets
⌃⌘G doesn't cycle on a retyped number
Taliessin through Logres: no page labels, the last page's notes as ::: note fences on their poems
detail: Asked: review the formatting of Williams, or perhaps older works in general (22:17): "The fact that the two Williams pieces I looked at have this problem suggest that it's a wider problem." Begun as S13 on Taliessin through Logres: "none of the pages have both prose and verse, so there it should probably just be 'Line ____', and the notes on the final page should probably be turned into ::: note fences on the poems they refer to. And we probably don't need page numbers at all." Also: "all the italic lines in the poems in Taliessin through Logres are part of the poem and should have line numbers (so <line>)." Victorian Narrative Verse "has hard-coded line numbers at the ends of lines, and footnotes to verse before the ::: note block existed so probably needs to be reformatted" (not read all the way through). Why: page labels give 44 Williams entries a Line-or-Page bar (MEASURED), notes sit apart from what they gloss, italic lines of the poems go unnumbered, and typed line numbers stand in the text; two works read, both with these, so likely more. Done when: the older works' formatting is surveyed (which works, which faults, counted over the backup), each fault has a decided form, and one-offs' import folders set them right, each review page read before import.

title: Helium bookmarks: "the bar did not show" once in a whole run
detail: Asked: found while playing S6's Helium verdict at 17:28: the bookmarks section failed with 'the bar did not show' (selected 0) at 'fb over a selection'; alone it passed 3 of 3. Why: a step that fails once in a whole run blocks an approve and costs a replay. Done when: the step holds its selection's race and the whole run passes it, measured over several runs. Paused (18:34): not reproduced in 12 whole runs since 8874ab6, nor alone (3), slowed 4x and 8x (4), or with its module's sections (3); a ProseMirror focus race was probed and ruled out (30 of 30 kept). 8874ab6 makes the next failure print the page's last selection calls with their callers. Reactivates when: 'the bar did not show' appears in a Helium verdict run (npm run test:helium, verify, the pre-commit): the verdict starts S6.1 itself, its watch set by P4, the failing line as the start's note; then read its calls to find what emptied the selection. A direct node tools/helium-corner.ts run is not read.

title: ⌃⌘R on a work by paragraph read 'not landed' in both plays of one verdict
detail: Asked: found while A17.1.1 was verified (11:19, 2026-11-23). Why: the corner and the order run of one verdict both read no selection and no reference on the clipboard after Escape from the Go to toolbar on Augustine 2; two plays of the section alone and the next whole verdict did not. Done when: the cause is found (the caret hand-back after Escape landing after the scripted selection is the first guess, untested) and held by the step, or the race shown to be elsewhere. Probed (07:39): ProseMirror's 20 ms focus timer writing its selection back over one a script placed straight after Escape: 3 of 3 stood at 1x and at 10x; not shown. The order run at 4x read the section as approved.

title: The order run read "column marks" otherwise once, with all four runs at once
detail: Asked: found 15:17 (not asked), play 2 of three after data-said: the order run read the column marks section otherwise once; its received copy was removed when the next play passed, so what differed is not known. Then asked (16:13): 'Yes, do all three' and 'No sense in having flakes in the F list if we don't automatically wake up and notice when they fail again.' Done 16:14-16:25: the drag is aimed once the page has settled (it was aimed two frames after the entry opened); the clipboard is emptied before ⌃⌘R and read once the reference fills it (it was read two frames after); a failed run's print is kept under tools/out/helium-failed/; the verdict prints and hands the wake 'section read otherwise — <section>' for each section a failed run reads otherwise, and F4 watches 'section read otherwise — column marks'. Three whole plays passed after (82.27-86.43 s). Why: the cause is not found; the two holds are guesses from the step's shape. Done when: woken, its kept print read and its cause held; or the reader closes it after enough whole plays without it. Woke 20:33 (not asked), the verdict over U16's readings: the order run read 'column marks' otherwise, 'a paired line's English into the next line's Latin' selecting 'of monarch ancestors, o et prae' where the forward run selected through '…meum, T'; kept at tools/out/helium-failed/order-2026-11-23-203311.txt. The drag's selection, not an alert. Paused (07:50): the 4x sweep in 5 windows (tools/heliumThrottle.ts 4) read this step otherwise once, the drag ending two lines low; alone it read right at 4x, 6x and 10x, and in its window at 4x. Measured: every drag after the first starts under 'Reference copied to clipboard', which moves the text 50 px; held by aimable (the info and success alerts closed before a point is measured, b292795); the sweep then read it as approved in both orders. Its time running out mid-drag is inferred, not shown. Reactivates when: 'section read otherwise — column marks' prints in a verdict. Probed 11:05: the drag played 9 times three ways (alert standing, closed between aim and drag, aimable first), all as approved; the forced close moved nothing, the 50 px having been two alerts. Since 800eccd the selection is set from the text, not dragged, so a recurrence is not the aim.

title: No new tab opened for either external link in one order run
detail: Asked: found 14:02 (not asked), the verdict over W3: in the order run's window, ⌘-click on an external link and ⌃⌘Enter on one both printed 'a new tab's wait ran out after 5000 ms' and read newTab:false, where the corner run beside it opened both; two replays of the order run opened both. Kept at tools/out/helium-failed/order-2026-11-24-140243.txt. Why: both waits in one window ran out together, so the window, not one step, stopped seeing its new pages (inferred). Done when: woken, the window's state at the run-out read and the cause held; or the reader closes it. Paused (16:26, U21): not reproduced in 6 order plays at 4x and 8x or 4 corner plays at 6x and 8x. A fresh browser's first https: tab took 0.4-2.5 s (26 browsers: idle, 30 CPU spinners, example.org answered locally, a real 5-window play beside it), a file: tab under 90 ms: a renderer started for a new site, not the network; never near 5 s, so F8 was a hang of that window, not slowness (inferred). Probe tools/out/u21/tabs.ts. Reactivates when: a verdict prints 'a new tab's wait ran out'; the verdict now replays it itself (U20.1), so the pair lands in the ledger.
watch: a new tab's wait ran out

title: What stands below an author is a book, never a work
detail: Asked: 'It's a bookshelf, let's do book', then 'we could use work for a thing on the bookshelf', then 'This isn't right yet, and it's more complicated than you are proposing. I think we defer it for now.' Why: help and code say both book and work for what the bookshelf holds, and the code takes a work by position (src/store/conventions.ts:40, depth 2), so First Doctor under Doctor Who is a 'work'. Done when: the bookshelf's words decided with the reader, then GLOSSARY.md, help, code and tools renamed and the old words retired. Paused (17:55): found so far, from the backup: Book is also an edition's division (Paradise Lost/Book 1..12, 'by book, chapter, and paragraph', a stored directive); levels differ by root: Milton, John/Paradise Lost/Book 1 (author, work, part), Doctor Who/First Doctor/1-1 An Unearthly Child (root with 'by innermost title alone', a grouping by Doctor with ## Season headings, the serial), Dante/Commedia/Inferno/28 (102 entries four deep); the directives at the second level are read from whatever stands there. Reactivates when: the reader takes it up.

detail: Found while pairing the Phaedo: my Greek reader took each Stephanus offset before collapsing whitespace, so labels drifted into words ('χρείη π ⟨4d⟩ οιεῖν'). Every dialogue imported under U29.1 and U30 is affected.
